datasets.name: SWE-bench Lite
datasets.note: Lite is a subset of the SWE-bench full test split; expanding the full test split (swe-bench-test) covers Lite's instances too, but expand Lite explicitly as well so the coverage report names it.

datasets.name: SWE-bench (full test split)
datasets.note: Only the TEST split is blocked. The same dataset's train split (19,008 instances) is legitimate training material — the blocklist matches by instance/commit, never by dataset name alone.

datasets.name: SWE-bench Pro (public set)
datasets.note: Public set only (731 of 1,865; the commercial and held-out sets are private and cannot be expanded or trained on). Public-set repos are GPL-family — do not redistribute their code.

datasets.name: SWE-bench Multilingual
datasets.note: 300 tasks across 42 repos and 9 languages (C, C++, Go, Java, JS, TS, PHP, Ruby, Rust).

datasets.name: Terminal-Bench 2.0
datasets.note: Terminal-Bench tasks are identified by task-directory name, not git commits. Expand from a local checkout of the task registry: each task dir name becomes a blocked instance_id. Public reference solutions exist — never train on TB tasks or solutions.

datasets.name: Terminal-Bench 1.0
datasets.note: Task count varies by registry version — record the count you actually expanded in the coverage report.

extra_blocked.note: Hand additions that do not belong to a named dataset above (e.g. a Multi-SWE-bench, SWE-EVO, CrossCodeEval, RepoBench, AgentDojo, InjecAgent, RedCode, HarmBench or CyberSecEval instance — see dataset-catalog.md §6 for the full list of eval suites this blocklist must eventually cover). repo_commit_pairs entries are objects {"repo": "owner/name", "base_commit": "<full sha>"}.

honesty_note: SEED FILE. The instance_ids / base_commits arrays are intentionally EMPTY at seed time: this file ships the correct dataset identifiers, split names, expected counts, and (where they are public knowledge) the eval repo names, but it does NOT contain the thousands of per-instance IDs. Run `node blocklist.mjs expand <downloaded-dataset.jsonl> --dataset <id>` for each dataset after downloading it from its canonical source to populate instance-level coverage. Until a dataset is expanded, matching for it works at the dataset/repo level only and ingestion code must treat unexpanded datasets as 'unknown — verify manually', never as 'clean'. No instance ID in this project is ever written from memory or fabricated.
purpose: Every instance, repo+commit pair, and base-commit hash that belongs to an evaluation Mochi reports. Training-data ingestion MUST drop (and log) anything matching this file. See README.md in this directory and dataset-catalog.md §6.
